title: Laravel Routing – Basic to Advanced
objectives: Routing ka purpose aur request ka route tak ka safar samajhna
`Route::get()` aur baaki HTTP method routes likhna
Closure aur controller routes mein farak jaanna
Named routes banana aur `route()` helper se use karna
`php artisan route:list` se routes check karna
prerequisites: Laravel project install ho chuka ho (Module 02)

sections.heading: Routing kya hoti hai?
sections.body:
Jab browser mein koi URL khulta hai, Laravel ko decide karna padta hai ki **kaunsa code chalega**. Yeh decision routing karti hai. Simple bhasha mein: **URL + HTTP method** ko **code** se jodna.

Laravel mein saare web routes `routes/web.php` file mein likhe jaate hain.

callout.text: Route ko ek receptionist samjho: visitor (request) aata hai, receptionist dekhta hai kis department (controller/closure) ko bhejna hai.

sections.heading: Real-world example: E-commerce website
sections.body:
Ek online store mein yeh pages chahiye: Home, Products, Cart aur Checkout. Har page ka ek URL hota hai, aur har URL ke peeche ek route.

- `/` – Home page
- `/products` – Products list
- `/cart` – Customer ki cart
- `/checkout` – Order place karna (POST request)

sections.heading: Basic syntax
sections.body: Sabse chhota route ek URL aur ek closure leta hai. Neeche wala code edit karke dekho (PHP yahan run nahi hota, sirf practice ke liye).

code.code:
<?php

use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;

Route::get('/products', function () {
    return 'Product List';
});

explain: `Route::get()` – sirf HTTP GET request handle karta hai.
`function () {...}` – Closure hai, jo request aane par chalta hai.
`return 'Product List';` – Response browser ko wapas jaata hai.

sections.heading: Advanced example: controller aur named route
sections.body: Real projects mein closure ki jagah controller use hota hai, aur route ko ek **name** diya jaata hai taaki URL badle to poora code na badalna pade.

code.code:
<?php

namespace App\Http\Controllers;

class ProductController extends Controller
{
    public function show(string $id)
    {
        return "Product #{$id}";
    }
}

explain: `{id}` – route parameter hai, URL ka dynamic hissa.
`->name('products.show')` – route ka naam. `route('products.show', ['id' => 5])` sahi URL bana deta hai.

sections.heading: HTTP methods
sections.body:
Har action ke liye alag method:

- `Route::get()` – data padhna
- `Route::post()` – naya data bhejna (form submit)
- `Route::put()` / `Route::patch()` – update karna
- `Route::delete()` – delete karna
- `Route::any()` – koi bhi method

HTML form sirf GET aur POST bhejta hai. PUT, PATCH, DELETE ke liye form mein `@method('PUT')` likhna padta hai.

callout.text: Har POST form mein `@csrf` zaroor lagao, warna Laravel 419 error dega.

versionDiff.heading: Laravel 11, 12 aur 13 mein farak
versionDiff.intro: Routing ka syntax teeno versions mein lagbhag same hai. Farak project structure aur requirements mein hai.

items.11: Slim skeleton: sirf `routes/web.php` aur `routes/console.php` milte hain. API routes ke liye `php artisan install:api` chalao. Routing config `bootstrap/app.php` ke `withRouting()` mein hoti hai.
items.12: Routing syntax 11 jaisa hi hai, structure bhi same. PHP 8.2 ya upar.
items.13: Routing basics same. PHP 8.3 ya upar chahiye. Controllers par middleware aur policy checks PHP attributes se declare kar sakte ho (13 docs: `#[Middleware]`, `#[Authorize]`). Detail lesson 04 mein.

errors.cause: `route()` mein naam galat hai ya route par `->name()` nahi lagaya.
errors.fix: Naam check karo aur `php artisan route:list` chalao.

errors.cause: URL ya HTTP method route se match nahi hua.
errors.fix: URL ka spelling dekho. Agar routes cached hain to `php artisan route:clear` chalao.

errors.cause: Controller ka `use` statement missing hai ya naam galat hai.

debug.body: Routing ki problem mein sabse pehle saare registered routes dekho.

code.code:
php artisan route:list
php artisan route:list --name=products
php artisan route:clear

exercise.intro: `routes/web.php` mein yeh routes banao aur browser mein test karo:
tasks: Product route (`/products/{id}`) jo `ProductController@show` call kare, naam `products.show`

quiz.why: `Route::get()` sirf GET requests ko handle karta hai.

quiz.q: Saare registered routes dekhne ki command kaunsi hai?
quiz.why: `php artisan route:list` sab routes dikhata hai.

quiz.q: Named route ka fayda kya hai?
options: URL badle to code mein har jagah badalna nahi padta
quiz.why: `route('name')` URL khud bana deta hai, to URL badalne par sirf route definition badalni padti hai.

interview.a: Routing URL aur HTTP method ko closure ya controller action se map karti hai. Web routes `routes/web.php` mein hote hain.
GET data padhne ke liye hai aur URL mein parameters jaate hain. POST data bhejne ke liye hai (body mein) aur Laravel mein CSRF token chahiye.
Route ko `->name()` se naam dena, taaki `route('naam')` se URL generate ho.

interview.q: Closure route aur controller route mein kya farak hai?
interview.a: Closure chhote kaam ke liye theek hai. Controller organized rehta hai, aur `route:cache` bhi controller routes ke saath hi chalta hai.
URL ka dynamic hissa, jaise `/products/{id}`. Value controller ya closure ko argument ke roop mein milti hai.

summary: Routing URL + method ko code se jodti hai.
Controller routes aur named routes real projects mein standard hain.
Debugging ke liye `php artisan route:list` use karo.
Syntax 11, 12, 13 mein same hai. PHP requirement 13 mein 8.3 hai.
